primarySuggestion.name: DC01 Mild Steel Sheet
primarySuggestion.reasoning: Stage-1 classifier forces sheet_metal framing; deterministic strip/web math (3mm web) implies gauge ≤1.5mm, consistent with a mild steel sheet grade. However, geometry (mean wall 34mm, max 169.95mm, 44 undercuts, 132 cylinders, bosses to 57mm radius) is far more consistent with a cast/machined steel part than a stamping. Following guidance to prefer steel over aluminium for a dense, thick-section, likely structural component absent an explicit aluminium signal.

processRecommendations.reasoning: Per stage-1 pre-selection and mandated specialist framing; deterministic blank/strip/pitch values point to a 12-station progressive tool (1 blank + 25 bends + 1 pierce).

Geometry evidence (fill ratio 0.092, wall thickness range 0.45-169.95mm, 44 undercuts, 132 cylindrical/55 conical/34 toroidal faces, bosses to 57mm) is strongly inconsistent with a flat-pattern stamped part and instead matches a cast, thick-section component requiring secondary machining.
High free-form content (76 B-spline faces) and undercuts could alternatively be produced by multi-axis milling if volumes were low; less likely at 200k units/yr.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Large undercut count is incompatible with simple open/close stamping dies; would require complex cams/side-actions or is evidence the part is not truly sheet metal.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Re-verify process selection with actual drawing/photo; if stamped, redesign to eliminate undercuts or split into multiple formed shells.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: A 375:1 thickness ratio is impossible in a single-gauge sheet metal part.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Confirm with customer whether part is solid/cast; if sheet metal, uniform gauge must be specified.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: High bend count in one progressive tool increases springback stack-up and die complexity.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Simulate bend sequence and add relief features to control springback.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Holes close to bend radii risk distortion during forming.

dfmIssues.description: Wall thickness spans 0.45mm to 169.95mm (mean 34mm) with 44 undercuts and 55 conical/34 toroidal faces — this is not achievable as a single-gauge stamped sheet metal part.
dfmIssues.impact: If forced into a progressive die, most of the part's volume/features cannot be formed, leading to tooling redesign, scrap, and project failure.
dfmIssues.fix: Confirm actual process with the customer's drawing/photo; if the part is genuinely solid/cast, switch commodityType to casting or cast_and_machine.

dfmIssues.description: 44 undercut faces cannot be released from a simple 2-directional stamping die.
dfmIssues.impact: Requires cam-actuated slides or secondary forming stations, materially raising die cost beyond the £30k progressive-die estimate.
dfmIssues.fix: Split geometry into multiple stamped/welded sub-assemblies or move to casting where side-cores are standard.

dfmIssues.description: High bend count within one strip increases cumulative springback and dimensional drift across stations.
dfmIssues.impact: Increased first-off tuning time, higher scrap during ramp-up, tighter die maintenance intervals.
dfmIssues.fix: Group bends into progressive stages with over-bend compensation and add coining stations at critical bends.

dfmIssues.description: 21 pierced holes, several near tight bend radii, risk elongation/tearing during forming.
dfmIssues.impact: Hole tolerance drift and localized cracking, causing rework or scrap.
dfmIssues.fix: Relocate holes ≥3× thickness from bend lines or pierce after forming in a secondary station.

dfmIssues.description: Threads cannot be formed in-die and require secondary tapping or PEM insertion.
dfmIssues.impact: Adds secondary operation cost and cycle time not captured in base stamping cycle.
dfmIssues.fix: Add dedicated tapping/insert station to the line or use self-clinching fasteners.

analysis.aiExplanation: The part was routed to me as a sheet-metal specialist per Stage-1 classification, and I've populated all sheet-metal cost fields (thickness, die cost, die life, process, net weight, shear strength) using steel as the ground-truth material per the guidance to prefer steel over aluminium for dense, thick-section components absent an explicit aluminium signal. However, the underlying OCCT geometry (0.45-169.95mm wall range, fill ratio 0.092, 44 undercuts, 132 cylindrical + 55 conical + 34 toroidal faces, bosses to 57mm radius, threaded features) is strongly inconsistent with a true stamped sheet-metal part and instead matches a cast/machined steel component. I've flagged this mismatch as a Critical DFM issue and recommend the customer confirm the actual manufacturing route before tooling investment. All deterministic geometry, cycle-time, and parametric tooling figures were used verbatim as instructed.
analysisLimitations: Stage-1 sheet_metal classification (conf 0.9) conflicts with strong geometric evidence for casting/machining (fill ratio 0.092, extreme wall thickness range, 44 undercuts) — recommend manual review of source drawing/photo.
Sheet gauge (1.5mm assumed) was inferred from the deterministic web-margin formula, not from a stated material spec — true gauge is unknown.
Net weight (8.141kg) is based on true solid volume at steel density, which is only meaningful if the part is genuinely a solid/cast steel body rather than a thin formed shell.
Die life and shear strength values are rule-of-thumb estimates for generic mild steel (DC01), not verified against an actual spec.

dfmIssues.description: 25 bends per part — Many bends multiply press-brake handling, tool changes and cumulative angle tolerance.
dfmIssues.fix: Reduce bend count, group same-tool bends, or move to a stamping die if volume supports it.

deterministicAnalysis.aiExplanation:
Derived deterministically for sheet_metal from the measured geometry. No AI call was made; every figure below is arithmetic on a measurement or a library lookup, and each states its own basis.

  • sheetMetal.blankLengthMm = 291 — largest bounding-box dimension × 1.05 trim allowance [geometry, sm-blank-l]
  • sheetMetal.blankWidthMm = 234 — second-largest bounding-box dimension × 1.05 trim allowance [geometry, sm-blank-w]
  • sheetMetal.numOps = 12 — 1 blank + 25 bend(s) + 1 pierce = 12 stations [geometry, sm-num-ops]
  • sheetMetal.strokesPerMin = 31 — feed-limited: 18 m/min ÷ 294 mm pitch, de-rated for 25 bends [rule, sm-spm]

Still open (1):
  • What is this part made of? — A CAD file carries shape, not substance. We measured 1037 cm³ exactly, but the same solid weighs 2.80 kg in aluminium and 8.14 kg in steel. Nothing in the geometry distinguishes them, and guessing wrong moves the material cost several-fold.
analysisLimitations: Unanswered: What is this part made of?

DFM checks ran against the measured geometry. Checks that need a drawing callout — tolerances, which face is critical, whether a weld line is in a load path — did not run, so this list is a floor and not a ceiling.
